subject: Post-demo: Hosted quickstart scope & endpoint/rate clarifications
content:
Message 1
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Mercado <ellie@shopwise.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@shopwise.com>
Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Hosted quickstart scope & endpoint/rate clarifications

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Highlights from the demo
- Confirmed target flows: chat-based product recommendations (short context, ~150 tokens response) and nightly batch embeddings for search reindexing.
- Expected burst pattern: interactive peak during day (spiky, ~180–220 rps for search autocomplete), batch windows overnight for embeddings.

Key open questions I captured
1) Can Redwood Hosted support a sandbox that mimics the peak ~200 rps pattern and what are the expected rate limits?
2) How does prefix/KV caching behave on Hosted — will it reduce token cost for repeated prompts?
3) Rough cost and SLO expectations for a 3-week evaluation pilot (hosted endpoints + sample traffic).

Attachments: demo recording, a sample traffic CSV you provided, and our Hosted quickstart checklist (attached).

Proposed next steps
- I’ll provision a sandbox hosted endpoint and share keys (ETA: 24 hours).
- Chloe (cc’d) will add an ops checklist and a short note on caching/throughput knobs.
- Suggest a follow-up ops call: Thu 5/7 10:00am PT to walk the team through traffic slicing and rate parachute.

If any of the bullets above are off, flag them and I’ll correct.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---

Message 2
From: Ellie Mercado <ellie@shopwise.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@shopwise.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted quickstart scope & endpoint/rate clarifications

Thanks Camila — that recap is helpful. A couple clarifying questions before we jump into a sandbox: 

- Rate profile: the 180–220 rps peak is correct for autocomplete at launch, but sustained peaks will be short (60–120s) and mostly GET-like pattern (stateless). Can Hosted handle short sustained bursts to 220 rps without queueing?
- Caching: we rely heavily on prefix reuse for product name completions. Does Redwood Hosted expose prefix/KV caching behavior (TTL, shard locality) so we can estimate token savings?
- Security/region: can the hosted sandbox be placed in us-west region and have audit logs for requests? We'll need logs for our security review.

Also — for the embeddings batch: we won't exceed 50k tokens/hour during the trial.

Would love the sandbox creds and a short note on rate ceilings you expect to enforce. If Thu 5/7 10am PT works for you, we'll take it.

Cheers,
Ellie Mercado
Head of Search & Personalization
Shopwise

----

Message 3
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Mercado <ellie@shopwise.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@shopwise.com>
Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted quickstart scope & endpoint/rate clarifications

Thanks Ellie — answers inline below, and I attached the Hosted quickstart checklist with sandbox details.

- Bursty peaks to 220 rps: Hosted supports short burst windows; for a sandbox we'll provision a perf-slice that tolerates 250 rps bursts for the duration of the trial. There are two caveats: 1) the sandbox routing has conservative default ratecaps to protect multi-tenant isolation; we will raise that cap for Shopwise during the pilot; 2) very long sustained peaks (multi-minute sustained at max) will be reviewed — but your 60–120s pattern is fine.

- Caching/prefix reuse: Hosted provides automatic prefix (KV) caching where applicable. We expose metrics for cache hit rate and approximate token savings in the Console. TTLs are currently set per model variant (default 5m) but we can adjust TTL for the sandbox to demonstrate savings. Note: prefix caching is most effective when prompts reuse long common prefixes — it won't help for truly ad-hoc queries.

- Region & audit logs: yes — sandbox will be in us-west-2. We will enable request-level audit logs and a link to a temporary retention view in the Console for the pilot (searchable by request id). Long-term retention/archival for production requires an enterprise add-on; we'll note that in the checklist.

Sandbox plan (what we'll provide in 24h)
- 1 hosted endpoint (chat/generation) pinned to a 7B quantized variant for cost/latency balance.
- 1 embeddings endpoint for overnight jobs.
- Rate ceiling: baseline 100 rps, elevated to 250 rps for 72h window on request. We can tweak after we validate traffic shape.
- Prefetch/prefix cache: TTL bumped to 10m for the sandbox so you can see impact.

Attachments included: hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (contains the keys, sandbox endpoints, and a short runbook), and a short sample-traffic csv with suggested slicing for the ops call.

Chloe — can you add a 10–15 minute ops walkthrough slide in the doc so Shopwise knows where to look for cache metrics?

Ben — can you confirm whether we can offer a 30% pilot credit on tokens for Shopwise (deal_id SW-2026-0421) if they commit to the three-week evaluation?

Thanks — will follow up with credentials in a separate secure notes email.

Best,
Camila

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Ellie Mercado <ellie@shopwise.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@shopwise.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted quickstart scope & endpoint/rate clarifications

Thanks — quick note from pricing/ops side. 30% pilot credit sounds fine to me for a short evaluation; I'll mark the credit on the deal and add a 10k token safety buffer to the sandbox billing profile so we don't hit hard gates during the first 48h.

Next steps (ops + commercial)
- Camila: send sandbox creds via secure notes and attach the quickstart PDF (avoid putting keys on the thread).
- Chloe: include the 10–15 slide ops walkthrough and a short video clip pointing at the cache metrics in Console.
- Schedule: Thu 2026-05-07 10:00am PT confirmed for the ops runbook call. Invite sent by calendar (accept/decline shows).

I'll also add a short DocuSign link for the pilot terms (simple SS trial T&Cs) — no enterprise contract yet, just a pilot agreement for audit and billing.

Ben Carter
Head of Solutions & Pricing
Redwood Inference
